title: Detective SAM: Adaptive AI-Image Forgery Localization
claim: On a state-of-the-art edit, baseline detectors miss or misplace the tampered region while ours closely matches the ground-truth mask.
layout: 1 row, 8 columns, left-to-right, highlighted yellow box around ours
description: A single horizontal strip of eight image columns, each with a bold title above. From left: the original painting (girl with a blue headscarf), the tampered version with a banana-pattern headscarf and a red arrow between them, and a black-and-white ground-truth mask showing the edited headscarf in white. Next is Detective SAM, outlined in a yellow box, with a red overlay filling the headscarf. Four baselines follow: FakeShield, TruFor, SAFIRE and Mesorch. FakeShield partly covers the scarf, TruFor spills over the face and scatters red spots, and SAFIRE and Mesorch show only tiny red specks. A white instruction caption, 'Change the headdress to a banana pattern.', sits at the bottom left. The eye goes first to the yellow-boxed column and its bright red mask.
caption: For a NanoBanana sample: original image, tampered image, Ground-Truth (GT) mask, Detective SAM (ours) and baseline mask predictions, limited to models that produced output, for all models see Appendix B.1.
abstract: Image forgery localization in the generative AI era poses new challenges, as modern editing pipelines produce photorealistic, semantically coherent manipulations that evade conventional detectors while model capabilities evolve rapidly. In response, we develop Detective SAM, a framework built on SAM2, a foundation model for image segmentation, that integrates perturbation-driven forensic clues with lightweight feature adapters and a mask adapter to convert forensic clues into forgery masks via automatic prompting. Moreover, to keep up with the rapidly evolving capabilities of diffusion models, we introduce AutoEditForge: an automated diffusion edit generation pipeline spanning four edit types. This supplies high-quality data to maintain localization accuracy under newly released editors and enables continual fine-tuning for Detective SAM. Across seven benchmark datasets and seven baselines, Detective SAM delivers stable out-of-distribution performance, averaging 36.99 IoU / 44.19 F1, a 33.67% relative IoU gain over the best baseline. Further, we show that state-of-the-art edits cause localization systems to collapse. With 500 AutoEditForge samples, Detective SAM quickly adapts and restores performance, enabling practical, low-friction updates as editing models improve. The pretrained weights, AutoEditForge, and evaluation script are available at https://github.com/Gertlek/DetectiveSAM
